title: Splitwise users, groups, expenses
idea: A Splitwise model records who paid and who owes which part: users belong to groups, and each expense is one immutable payment divided into shares.

analogy.text: A shared house notebook. Each line says who paid, the total, and each housemate's part. Only housemates appear in it.
analogy.breaks: A notebook takes any scribble; the model rejects lines that do not add up.

points: Users and groups live long; an `Expense` is a frozen record of one payment.
Money is `long` cents: integer sums are exact, so shares can match totals.
An `Expense` guards its own invariants: positive total, shares summing to it.
`Group` checks membership, because only the group knows who belongs to it.

steps.caption: A `Group` has members. Users exist on their own and can join many groups.
The group records expenses. Adding one is where membership is checked.
An `Expense` names one payer and a total in cents. It never changes after creation.
The total is divided into `Share` values, one per person who owes a part.
How shares are computed (equal, exact, percent) is a strategy, kept out of `Expense`.
Balances are derived from expenses, never typed in. That keeps one source of truth.

code.title: The problem: loose data
code.caption: Open fields, `double` money and no checks: outsiders owe, shares miss, history changes.

walk.text: Package-visible lists: any code in the package can add members or expenses unchecked.
Money is a `double`, and shares are a loose map keyed by display name.
Zed is not a member, yet the share is stored.
Nothing compares the shares with the amount. The printout shows the gap.
Chen ate dinner but owes nothing, and the model cannot notice.
A recorded expense changes in place, so past balances change silently.

code.title: The fix: guarded model
code.caption: Records for values, cents for money, and each object guarding the rule it can check.

walk.text: Small value types. A `Share` is never negative; a `User` always has an id.
An expense is a record. `List.copyOf` freezes the shares the caller passed in.
The invariant lives with the data: shares must add up to the total, to the cent.
Group state is private. Members are kept by id, in insertion order.
The group checks the payer and every share holder, since only it knows members.
Callers get a copy, so nobody adds an unchecked expense behind the group's back.
One valid dinner, a taxi whose shares fall short, and a boat ride with an outsider.

pitfalls: Storing money as `double` lets shares drift from the total; store `long` cents.
Editing a recorded expense rewrites history; add a correcting expense or a new version.
Putting every check in one `ExpenseService` breeds a god class; let objects guard their rules.

quiz.q: Same classes as the fix. What does this print?
quiz.why: The compact constructor stored `List.copyOf(parts)`, a separate unmodifiable copy. Adding to the caller's `ArrayList` later cannot reach the expense.

takeaway: Model money in cents, freeze expenses, and let each object guard its rules.

starters: Should Group or an ExpenseService own the list of expenses?
How do I handle expenses in different currencies?
How would I let a user edit an expense without rewriting history?
